name: Louisa Macartney Crawford
bio: Louisa Macartney Crawford was a contributor to Chapman and Hall’s Metropolitan Magazine from about 1835, where she published a series of autobiographical sketches.

She wrote the words for several books of songs set by the composer F. Nicholls Crouch; “Kathleen Mavourneen” appeared in the first of the series, Echoes from the Lakes. The poem here is taken from Edmund Clarence Stedman’s A Victorian Anthology, 1837–1895 (1895).

poems.title: Kathleen Mavourneen
poems.author: Louisa Macartney Crawford
poems.collection: A Victorian Anthology, 1837–1895, ed. Edmund Clarence Stedman (1895)
poems.text:
Kathleen Mavourneen! the gray dawn is breaking,
The horn of the hunter is heard on the hill;
The lark from her light wing the bright dew is shaking,—
Kathleen Mavourneen! what, slumbering still?
Oh, hast thou forgotten how soon we must sever?
Oh! hast thou forgotten this day we must part?
It may be for years, and it may be forever!
Oh, why art thou silent, thou voice of my heart?
Oh! why art thou silent, Kathleen Mavourneen?

Kathleen Mavourneen, awake from thy slumbers!
The blue mountains glow in the sun’s golden light;
Ah, where is the spell that once hung on my numbers?
Arise in thy beauty, thou star of my night!
Mavourneen, Mavourneen, my sad tears are falling,
To think that from Erin and thee I must part!
It may be for years, and it may be forever!
Then why art thou silent, thou voice of my heart?
Then why art thou silent, Kathleen Mavourneen?
